Where agents run · required
  A computer of yours: agents run on it directly.
<QR>
  1. A computer
     The workspace's own machine can run agents too. In the app, Settings › Workspace › Machines › Add machine does each of these.
     The workspace's own machine, on it:
       fleetd machine add --local
     Another machine, on the workspace's machine:
       fleetd pair --worker <name>
       The workspace is only at http://HUB, which no other machine reaches, so only a node on the workspace's own computer can join it. For another machine, give the workspace its tailnet or LAN address: on the workspace's machine, run fleetd init --listen <ip>:<port> --url http://<name>:<port> (Settings › Workspace › Setup › Where the workspace listens), then try again.
<QR>
  2. Android screens (optional)
     Android emulators run on any Linux machine with KVM: the first one installs itself. iOS simulators are the agents' Mac's: A Mac for agents sets it up.
<QR>
  In the app: Settings › Workspace › Machines.
<QR>
  Test: Read each computer's checks.
✗  Where agents run required: A computer of yours: agents run on it directly

Run fleetd init --step machines again when you've done it; it keeps what's done.
